summary: Keep order-independent range digests of the claims each store retains

replay.detail: No replay. A background job (maintenance.claim_ranges) folds existing claims into the digests once, 4,096 claims per background writer loan with a committed cursor, resting outside the loan for max(100 ms, 4 x the loan's hold), capped at 5 s; it resumes after a restart. Later claim inserts and deletes queue by trigger and fold after each store event.

schema.detail: Adds claim_range_digests (WITHOUT ROWID), claim_range_pending, claim_range_import and two plain-SQL triggers on claims (AFTER INSERT, AFTER DELETE) that queue each change. Storage version stays 20. Measured with crates/smallclaims/examples/claim_ranges_bench.rs (release build, file-backed store, 1,000,000 claims): the digests occupy 380,928 B whatever the claim count, since 4,096 leaves and 64 tops bound them; the queue holds 76.0 B per unfolded claim and empties as the job folds it. Rollback leaves the tables and triggers in place; the triggers call no application function, so an earlier binary's claim writes succeed and queue their changes for the next capable build to fold.

rules.detail: Nothing reads the digests yet: replication, admission, checkpoints and projections are unchanged. They are transport summaries for claims-range sync, not authentication.

compatibility.detail: No wire, client or backup format change. The digests are local storage; a restore rebuilds them through the triggers and the import.

downtime.detail: Normal restart; the open records the import bound in one savepoint. Same bench, two runs on a loaded build host: admitting 1,000,000 claims in 10,000-claim transactions took 131.8 s without the triggers and 127.8 s with them, so the queue insert is within this host's noise. Trimming 500,000 claims took 73.9 vs 82.1 us/claim in the first run and 80.4 vs 79.9 in the second. Folding 1,000,000 queued inserts took 245 background loans, hold p50 19.5-30.6 ms, p99 44.8-66.0 ms, max 52.2-79.3 ms, 5.7-8.9 s of writer work in total; folding 500,000 deletes took 123 loans, max hold 51.5-56.9 ms. These are synthetic measurements, not production bounds.

recovery.detail: Swapping back to an earlier binary is supported: its claim writes keep queuing, and a later capable build folds the queue. Nothing depends on the digests yet.
